narrative.northStar: Ant Design v5's language as plain CSS tokens
narrative.overview:
Ant Design v5's language, written as plain CSS custom properties in src/styles/global.css. There is no React and no antd package: the tokens at the top of that file are the whole system, and every component style in the site is built from them. Ant supplies the palette, the neutral scale, the radii, the elevation, the control heights and the button, card, list, menu, anchor and table shapes. IBM Plex supplies the letterforms, because it is self-hosted and has a matching Korean cut.

The site is flat until something is a card. A card at rest is a 1px #f0f0f0 border on the container's white, with no shadow; the showcase card on the front page is the one surface elevated at rest, because it is what the page is about. Colour on a page comes from the shaders: the chrome holds one blue and one red, and the greys carry everything else.

Dark is Ant's dark algorithm, with the link and rail blue lifted one step so it clears 4.5:1 on the #141414 ground. Motion is Ant's single 0.2s curve on hover and press. The shaders move; the chrome does not.
keyCharacteristics: Ant Design v5 tokens as plain CSS custom properties, no React and no antd package
One blue (#1677ff) and one red (#ff4d4f); every other colour is a grey
Three radii: 4px on a tag, 6px on a control, 8px on a card or code frame
Flat at rest, elevated on state, with the showcase card the one exception
IBM Plex Sans and Mono, self-hosted, with a Korean cut at 400 and 600
Three measures: the 1200px container, the 740px document column, the 960px wide figure

rules.name: The Two Families Rule
rules.body: Plex Sans carries interface and prose; Plex Mono carries code, identifiers, diagnostics, the version tag, the layout table and a uniform's own field name. A word that names something the compiler reads is set in the mono face wherever it appears.

rules.name: The Single Blue Rule
rules.body: The page has one blue and one red. A new state finds its colour in the primary's own wash (#e6f4ff), border (#91caff) or text hover (#69b1ff) before it introduces a hue.

rules.name: The Resting Flat Rule
rules.body: A surface earns its shadow from state or from being the one thing the page is about. The showcase card is elevated at rest because it is the page's subject; a tile, a pager and a table row are flat until the pointer is on them.

rules.name: The Container Rule
rules.body: A full-width page is laid out in the 1200px container with the gutters; a page of prose is laid out in the 740px column. A third measure needs a reason.

dos: Do build a new surface from the tokens at the top of src/styles/global.css; both palettes live there and nowhere else.
Do use the default button face for everything but the page's own action, which is the filled face at the large size (40px, 16px text, 8px radius).
Do give a card a 1px #f0f0f0 border, an 8px radius and 16px of body padding, and let the elevation shadow arrive on hover as the border goes transparent.
Do set interface text at 14px and prose at 16px, with headings at 38, 30, 24, 20 and 16px, each at weight 600.
Do put every canvas over its build-time still, so the frame is never empty.
Do keep the one transition: 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.645, 0.045, 0.355, 1) on colour, border, background and shadow.
donts: Don't add a third hue. The chrome has one blue and one red, and the colour on a page comes from the shaders.
Don't use a colour gradient, a glow or a coloured card border.
Don't write a utility class into the markup. Tailwind is kept for its @theme tokens and preflight.
Don't put a resting shadow on a surface that is not the page's subject.
Don't invent a fourth radius or a fourth measure.
Don't set a label in capitals, a tracked eyebrow line above a heading, or a metadata string joined by middle dots.
